opener: A labour shed is the open-hall version of SAMAN worker housing: one clear sleeping hall per floor with central aisles, built as a light portal-frame steel building with PPGI cladding and high-level ventilation. It suits contractors who need the highest bed count per rupee and manage the hall as one space. The hall comes in six sizes, 60x24 ft G+1 up to 120x24 ft G+2, sleeping 58 to 216 workers a building. The hall is priced ex-factory on one per-square-foot rate, delivered in 7 to 21 working days with zoned lighting and emergency circuits fitted.
descriptionHtml:
The Labour Shed: Maximum Beds, One Open Hall

The labour shed is built around a single idea: house the most workers in one supervised space for the least money. Every floor is one clear hall with no internal walls, facing bed rows split by an aisle that runs end to end. A light portal frame keeps the span open, PPGI cladding keeps weather out, and ventilator banks up high keep air crossing the hall without fans fighting the heat alone.

Why an Open Hall Works

Because the hall is one space, running it is simple in ways room blocks cannot match. From the doorway one supervisor counts every bed. Cleaning is one crew, one pass. Moving beds between crews is a list change, not a room change. Exits, emergency lighting and zoned circuits are engineered for open-hall occupancy from the first drawing, which is what separates a compliant shed from a shed-shaped problem.

120x24 ft G+28,640 sq ft173 to 216Rs 59,09,760

The two G+2 entries stack a third hall on the same land, the route to density when the plot cannot grow.

The Structure Behind the Hall

A portal or truss frame in light steel carries the clear span, so no post interrupts the bed rows. Double-slope or single-slope PPGI roofing sheds rain fast, an RCC slab is preferred under high occupancies, and the cladding takes an insulated upgrade where summers demand it. Every component row sits in the Specifications tab, written from the factory build standard rather than marketing copy.

Who Chooses the Shed

Contractors housing large homogeneous crews on civil packages, where beds per rupee is the whole equation and the crew is managed as shifts rather than gangs. Seasonal workforces suit it too: the hall re-assigns beds overnight, free of room administration. If your site needs lockable rooms instead, the hutment room block serves that brief; if the housing must travel between projects, the relocatable camp build does; and the worker housing range weighs all three on one page.

Shed Pricing

One rate, Rs 684 per square foot ex-GST, across all six sizes. No premium appears at the larger entries, so cost per bed actually falls as the hall grows. Freight and any fit-out are itemised separately on the quotation, which arrives fixed within 48 hours.

From Order to Occupied

Fabricated components leave the factory 7 to 21 working days after drawings are approved, and the hall stands in days on a prepared base. Staged handover is normal: the ground hall opens while the upper floor is still being fitted. Structure is warranted 5 years, finishing 1 year, as standard.

Why Order the Shed From SAMAN

We are the manufacturer, so hall length, ventilator count and exit positions flex at drawing stage without a middleman markup. Two factories serve north and south, 3,000+ customers have bought from them, and the same flat-rate discipline covers every building we sell.

Labour Shed FAQs

How many workers fit one shed?

58 up to 216 by the planning norm depending on size; the hall layout drawing fixes the number.

Can the hall be partitioned later?

Light partitions can be added, but if rooms are the plan, the hutment block builds them properly from day one.

What base does the shed need?

Compacted ground carries the smaller halls; RCC slabs are recommended at high occupancy and always at G+2.

Is the shed hot in summer?

High-level ventilators move air continuously, and insulated cladding is available where the climate needs it.

How fast can beds be ready?

Dispatch lands 7 to 21 working days after approval, then days of erection; the schedule comes with the quote.
